heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷三 · 7 · 納幣 … 乃易服不食

items.text: When he marries, charge him to meet his wife, carry on the family's ancestral rites, and be respectful and faithful.
items.quote: 往迎爾相承我宗事勉率以敬若則有常 — Go to meet your mate, carry on our ancestral rites, be diligent and respectful, and be constant.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry; no one may command it.

items.text: When giving her in marriage, instruct her to respect and obey her parents-in-law day and night, never disobeying their commands.
items.quote: 敬之戒之夙夜無違爾舅姑之命 — Be respectful and cautious; day and night never disobey your parents-in-law's commands.

items.text: On the morning after the wedding, present yourself to your parents-in-law, bow, and offer them your gift.
items.quote: 婦夙興盛服俟見舅姑...拜舅升奠贄幣 — The wife rises early, dresses formally, waits to see parents-in-law, bows and places gift-money.

items.text: If you are the wife of the eldest son, serve food and drink to your parents-in-law at mealtime.
items.quote: 若冡婦則饋於舅姑...婦盥升自西階洗盞斟酒置舅卓子上 — If she is the eldest son's wife, she presents food to parents-in-law; she washes, ascends, fills a cup, and places it on the father-in-law's table.

items.text: Receive your son's wife with the ceremonial courtesy and entertain her with a feast.
items.quote: 舅姑禮之...舅姑饗之 — The parents-in-law honor her... the parents-in-law feast her.

items.text: Pay respects to all the elders of your husband's household who are senior to your parents-in-law.
items.quote: 婦見於諸尊長...同居有尊於舅姑者則舅姑以婦見於其室 — The wife is presented to the various respected elders; if there are elders senior to the parents-in-law, they present her in their room.

items.text: Three days after the wedding, present your wife at the ancestral shrine to inform the ancestors.
items.quote: 三日主人以婦見於祠堂 — On the third day, the master presents the wife at the ancestral shrine.
items.conflict: Offerings to ancestors are idolatry; the living owe worship to God alone.

items.text: The day after the wedding, visit your wife's parents, bow to them, and bring gifts of introduction.
items.quote: 明日壻往見婦之父母...拜即跪而扶之入見婦母...皆有幣 — Next day the groom goes to see his wife's parents; he bows, then kneels and is helped up; he sees the wife's mother; all have gifts.

items.text: When someone has died, climb to the roof and call the soul back three times, then cover the body with the garment.
items.quote: 升屋中霤北面招以衣三呼曰某人復...卷衣降覆尸上 — Climb to the roof, face north, call with the garment three times, saying 'So-and-so, return!'; then roll up the garment and cover the corpse.
items.conflict: Calling back the dead is superstition; Scripture forbids consulting the dead.

items.text: As chief mourner, preside over the funeral offerings and rites for your deceased parent.
items.quote: 立喪主...凡主人謂長子無則長孫承重以奉饋奠 — Appoint the chief mourner: the eldest son, or eldest grandson if no son, takes responsibility to perform the offerings.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are idolatrous; mourning should not include sacrifice.

items.text: During mourning, abstain from eating for three days.
items.quote: 諸子三日不食 — The sons do not eat for three days.

items.text: As a widow, let down your hair, remove your ornaments, and wear mourning clothes.
items.quote: 妻子婦妾皆去冠及上服被髪 — Wives, children, daughters-in-law, and concubines all remove caps and outer garments and let down their hair.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 8 · 治棺 … 設奠狊

items.text: Have a coffin made of good wood, not too large or high, and line it with lacquer and asphalt.
items.quote: 油杉為上柏次之土杉為下其制方直頭大足小僅取容身勿令高大

items.text: Send word of the death to relatives and friends; receive condolences only after the wailing period.
items.quote: 訃告於親戚僚友

items.text: Have the body bathed and hair dressed, and bury the wash water, combs, and napkins in a pit.
items.quote: 乃沐浴...其沐浴餘水巾櫛棄於坎而埋之

items.text: Dress the dead in fresh clothes, removing the garments worn in illness.
items.quote: 悉去病時衣及復衣易以新衣

items.text: Set out offerings of dried meat and sauce, with wine, before the body.
items.quote: 執事者以卓子置脯醢升自阼階祝盥手洗盞斟酒奠於尸東
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead (Deut 26:14; 1 Cor 10:20)

items.text: All who should wear mourning take their places by rank and wail; those in deepest mourning sleep by the corpse.
items.quote: 主人以下為位而哭...三年之喪夜則寢於尸旁藉槀枕塊

items.text: Place rice and a coin in the mouth, on the right, left, and center.
items.quote: 以匙抄米實於尸口之右并實一錢又於左於中亦如之
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead (Deut 26:14)

items.text: Set up the spirit seat with a soul cloth of white silk, and place daily toilet articles as in life.
items.quote: 結白絹為魂帛置倚上設香爐香合珓杯注酒果於卓子上
items.conflict: Ancestor worship / spirit tablet (Ex 20:4-5; Lev 19:31)

items.text: Make a red silk banner inscribed with the deceased's name and rank, and stand it at the right of the spirit seat.
items.quote: 以絳帛為銘旌...書曰某官某公之柩

items.text: Perform no Buddhist services, masses, or offerings for the dead; they cannot help and only waste the estate.
items.quote: 不作佛事...世俗信浮屠誑誘

items.text: On the next day, dress the body in the lesser shroud, with cloth bands crosswise and lengthwise, but leave the face uncovered.
items.quote: 先布絞之横者三於下...未掩其面

items.text: On the third day, perform the greater dressing and place the body in the coffin; do not delay for divination of lucky days.
items.quote: 三日而歛...世俗以陰陽拘忌擇日而歛豈不悖哉

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 38 · 舉棺入置於堂中少西 … 五曰緦麻三月

items.text: Lean upon the coffin and weep to the full extent of grief.
items.quote: 主人主婦憑哭盡哀 — The master and his wife lean on the coffin and weep fully.

items.text: Do not place gold, jade, or valuables in the coffin, lest you stir robbers' hearts.
items.quote: 謹勿以金玉珍玩置棺中啟盜賊心 — Be careful not to place gold, jade, or valuables in the coffin, which stirs robbers' hearts.

items.text: Two women should remain and guard the spirit seat.
items.quote: 留婦人兩人守之 — Leave two women to guard it.
items.conflict: The spirit seat represents the dead person's soul; Christians should not venerate it.

items.text: Set out the offering as in the lesser dressing ceremony.
items.quote: 乃設奠〔如小歛之儀〕 — Then set out the offering, as in the lesser dressing ceremony.
items.conflict: Food offerings to the dead are not part of Christian worship.

items.text: When wearing unhemmed sackcloth for your father, sleep on straw, pillow on a clod, do not loosen the girdle, do not sit with others, and do not pass the inner gate except to see your mother.
items.quote: 寢苫枕塊不脱絰帶不與人坐 — Sleep on straw, clod pillow, keep girdle on, do not sit with others.

items.text: Women should stay in a separate room inside the inner gate or by the coffin, remove luxurious furnishings, and not go to men's mourning quarters.
items.quote: 去帷帳衾褥之華麗者不得輙至男子喪次 — Remove luxurious curtains and bedding; do not go to men's mourning quarters.

items.text: Wear unhemmed sackcloth for three years when your father dies.
items.quote: 其正服則子為父也 — The principal garment: a son for his father.

items.text: Wear unhemmed sackcloth for three years when your husband dies.
items.quote: 妻為夫也 — A wife for her husband.

items.text: Wear unhemmed sackcloth for three years when your husband's father dies.
items.quote: 婦為舅也 — A daughter-in-law for her husband's father.

items.text: Wear hemmed sackcloth for three years when your mother dies.
items.quote: 子為母也 — A son for his mother.

items.text: Wear one year's mourning (without staff) for grandparents.
items.quote: 為祖父母 — For grandparents.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷二 · 8 · 厥明宿興陳冠服 … 出以復書授使者遂禮之

items.text: Do not promise a child in marriage while still an infant or by pointing at the womb; wait until he is grown and examine his character and family conduct.
items.quote: 吾家男女必俟既長然後議昬 — In our family, boys and girls must wait until they are grown before marriage is discussed.

items.text: Send a matchmaker to the other house, and only after they agree proceed to the betrothal gifts.
items.quote: 必先使媒氏往來通言俟女氏許之然後納采 — First send a matchmaker back and forth; only after the woman's family consents then present the betrothal gifts.

items.text: Do not marry while in mourning of a year or more for a parent.
items.quote: 身及主昬者無期以上喪乃可成昬 — One who is in mourning of a year or more may not marry.

items.text: When a son is capped, present him at the ancestral hall to inform the ancestors.
items.quote: 主人以冠者見於祠堂 — The host takes the capped one to be seen at the ancestral hall.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment and the prohibition of necromancy.

items.text: When a betrothal is settled, report it at the ancestral hall.
items.quote: 夙興奉以告於祠堂 — Rise early and present the betrothal letter to the ancestors at the ancestral hall.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment and the prohibition of necromancy.

items.text: After the capping, bow to your parents and to all elders in the household, including elder brothers and sisters.
items.quote: 冠者北向拜父母 — The capped one faces north and bows to his parents.

items.text: If your son is not the eldest son of the main line, yield the presiding place to the clan head and stand at his right.
items.quote: 若非宗子之子則其父立於主人之右 — If he is not the son of the lineage heir, his father stands at the host's right.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 序 … 俗節則獻以時食

items.text: Guard the distinctions of name and rank, and make love and respect the substance of household life.
items.quote: 名分之守愛敬之實其本也 — The guarding of name and rank, the substance of love and respect, is the root.

items.text: Preserve the ancestral hall and its house intact from generation to generation; do not divide it.
items.quote: 凡祠堂所在之宅宗子世守之不得分析 — The house containing the ancestral hall the lineage heir must keep for generations and must not divide.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment.

items.text: Set aside sacrificial fields from the family land and manage them for the sacrifices; do not sell or pledge them.
items.quote: 毎龕取其二十之一以為祭田...不得典賣 — Take one-twentieth per niche for sacrificial fields; they must not be sold or pledged.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; also the inalienable land for idols.

items.text: Provide the vessels for sacrifice, store them under lock, and use them for nothing else.
items.quote: 具祭器...貯於庫中而封鎖之不得它用 — Provide sacrificial vessels, store them locked in the storeroom, do not use them for other purposes.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship.

items.text: If you are not the eldest legitimate son, do not preside over the sacrifice to your father; that belongs to the lineage heir.
items.quote: 非嫡長子則不敢祭其父 — One not the eldest legitimate son does not dare to sacrifice to his father.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; also denies the priesthood of all believers.

items.text: Go to the ancestral hall each morning, burn incense, and bow twice.
items.quote: 主人晨謁於大門之内...焚香再拜 — The master pays morning reverence within the main gate, burns incense and bows twice.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship, offering incense to the dead.

items.text: When leaving or returning, go to the hall, bow, and announce your departure or return to the ancestors.
items.quote: 出入必告...瞻禮而行歸亦如之 — Going out or coming in, announce; look and bow, and likewise on return.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; reporting to the dead.

items.text: Assemble before the tablets on the first and fifteenth of the month and at the solstices, and offer the full rites.
items.quote: 正至朔望則參 — At the solstices, new moon and full moon, hold the formal visitation.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship.

items.text: At seasonal festivals, offer the foods of the season to the ancestors.
items.quote: 俗節則獻以時食 — At customary festivals, present the foods of the season.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 80 · 作灰隔 … 祠后土於墓左

items.text: Build the grave securely with lime, charcoal, and boards so that the body may be preserved from soil, water, insects, and robbers.
items.quote: 作灰隔 ... 炭禦木根辟水蟻石灰得沙而實得土而黏歳乆結為全石螻蟻盜賊皆不能進也 — Make the lime layer... charcoal resists roots, water, ants; lime with sand hardens, with clay adheres; in years it becomes solid stone; ants and robbers cannot enter.

items.text: Inscribe a stone epitaph with the deceased's name, dates, and lineage, and place it near the grave so that if the grave is ever disturbed, the body may be recognized and covered again.
items.quote: 刻誌石 ... 其底叙年若干適某氏因夫子致封號無則否 ... 庶能為掩之也 — Inscribe the stone ... so that if the grave is disturbed, one may know his name and cover him again.

items.text: Make a spirit tablet and inscribe the name, and keep it in the ancestral hall for offerings.
items.quote: 作主 ... 以粉塗其前面 ... 夫婦俱入祠堂 — Make the tablet ... paint the front ... husband and wife both enter the ancestral hall.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20

items.text: Before the burial procession, present the coffin to the ancestors in the shrine, taking leave as one would before a journey.
items.quote: 奉柩朝於祖 ... 此禮盖象平生将出必辭尊者也 — Present the coffin to the ancestors ... this rite imitates taking leave of elders before going out.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20

items.text: Offer condolences and funeral gifts to the bereaved household.
items.quote: 親賓致奠賻〔如初喪儀〕 — Kin and guests present offerings and gifts, as at the first mourning.

items.text: Place the prescribed silk offerings in the grave as a final gift, and do not bury gold, jade, or other valuables that would burden the dead.
items.quote: 主人贈 ... 其餘金玉寳玩並不得入壙以為亡者之累 — The master presents ... other valuables must not be put in the grave, to avoid burdening the dead.

items.text: Set out the farewell offerings before the coffin leaves the house.
items.quote: 日晡時設祖奠 ... 乃設遣奠 — At evening set the farewell offering ... then set the departure offering.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead; Deut 26:14; Is 8:19-20

items.text: Carry the soul cloth and burn incense, guiding the spirit to the grave.
items.quote: 祝奉魂帛升車焚香 — The invoker carries the soul cloth, boards the carriage, and burns incense.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration; Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20

items.text: Offer sacrifice to the earth god at the left of the grave, for the peace of the burial place.
items.quote: 祠后土於墓左 — Sacrifice to the earth god at the left of the grave.
items.conflict: Worship of created spirits; Deut 4:19; 1 Cor 10:20

items.text: During transport, keep vigil by the coffin at night, with relatives guarding it.
items.quote: 夜則主人兄弟皆宿柩旁親戚共守衛之 — At night the master and brothers all sleep by the coffin, and relatives together guard it.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 119 · 藏明器等 … 叙立

items.text: Give your deceased parent a proper burial with the grave goods and a stone marker as the rites prescribe.
items.quote: 藏明器等 — Bury the grave goods and the like

items.text: Offer the three虞 sacrifices, the卒哭, and the祔 rite to settle the soul and place the spirit tablet among the ancestors.
items.quote: 孝子某奉祀 — The filial son offers the sacrifices
items.conflict: Second Commandment; worship God alone

items.text: As the principal wife, assist the son in the sacrificial offerings to the deceased parents-in-law, performing the亚献.
items.quote: 亞獻〔主婦為之禮如初 — The second offering: the principal wife performs it as before
items.conflict: Second Commandment; worship God alone

items.text: If you are the lineage heir and not the chief mourner, stand in the prescribed place and preside over the ancestral rite.
items.quote: 宗子主婦分立兩階之下 — The lineage heir and his wife stand apart below the two steps
items.conflict: Second Commandment; worship God alone

items.text: Observe the mourning abstinences according to your degree of kinship: abstain from wine, meat, and festive music for the prescribed period.
items.quote: 期九月之喪者飲酒食肉不與宴樂 — Those in one-year or nine-month mourning must not drink wine, eat meat, or join in feasts

items.text: After the final sacrifice, eat only vegetables and water, and sleep on a mat with a wooden pillow, in mourning for your parent.
items.quote: 主人兄弟蔬食水飲不食菜菓寢席枕木 — The sons eat only vegetables and drink water, and sleep on a mat with a wooden pillow

items.text: When leaving the grave, let elders mount their carriages first; only then may juniors ride.
items.quote: 尊長乘車馬去墓百歩許卑幼亦乘車馬 — Elders ride in carriages when 100 paces from the tomb; juniors also ride

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷一 · 32 · 凡父母舅姑有疾子婦無故不離側親調 … 陳設

items.text: When parents are ill, stay by their side, prepare and taste their medicine, call doctors, and set aside all other affairs until they recover.
items.quote: 父母有疾子色不滿容不戲笑不宴逰舎置餘事専以迎醫檢方合藥為務疾已復初 — When parents are ill, a son does not laugh or play, sets aside other affairs, and focuses on seeking doctors and preparing medicine.

items.text: When parents-in-law are ill, do not leave their side without reason; personally prepare and taste the medicine and serve it.
items.quote: 凡父母舅姑有疾子婦無故不離側親調嘗藥餌而供之 — When parents or parents-in-law are ill, sons and daughters-in-law without reason do not leave their side, personally adjust and taste the medicine and serve it.

items.text: Love what your parents love, and respect what they respect, even extending to animals, how much more to people.
items.quote: 凡子事父母父母所愛亦當愛之所敬亦當敬之 — In serving parents, love what they love and respect what they respect.

items.text: Gladden their hearts, do not oppose their will, please their senses, make their rest secure, and nourish them faithfully.
items.quote: 凡子事父母樂其心不違其志樂其耳目安其寢處以其飲食忠養之 — In serving parents, gladden their hearts, do not oppose their will, please their senses, make their rest secure, and nourish them faithfully.

items.text: If she is not yet respectful and filial, teach her patiently; if she cannot be taught, then be angry; if she cannot be angered, then whip; if after repeated whippings she still does not change, send away your son and expel her, but do not openly say she violated ritual.
items.quote: 屢笞而終不改子放婦出然亦不明言其犯禮也 — If after repeated whipping she still does not change, send away the son and expel the daughter-in-law, but do not openly say she violated ritual.

items.text: If your parents dislike your wife, divorce her; if you dislike her but your parents say she serves them well, maintain marital rites with her for life.
items.quote: 子甚宜其妻父母不悦出子不宜其妻父母曰是善事我子行夫婦之禮焉沒身不衰 — If a son loves his wife but parents dislike, divorce; if he dislikes her but parents say she serves well, maintain marital rites for life.
items.conflict: Bible: let no man separate what God has joined; husband and wife are one flesh (Matt 19:6).

items.text: Visit and greet elders morning and evening; rise when an elder passes; dismount when you meet an elder on the road; bow after an absence.
items.quote: 凡卑幼於尊長晨亦省問夜亦安置坐而尊長過之則起出遇尊長於塗則下馬 — Juniors greet elders morning and evening; when an elder passes, rise; when meeting on road, dismount.

items.text: Receive the bows of juniors with appropriate dignity: raise up a son-in-law or nephew, and stand to receive a grandson's bow.
items.quote: 凡受女壻及外甥拜立而扶之外孫則立而受之可也 — When receiving bow from son-in-law or nephew, stand and raise him; from grandson, stand and receive.

items.text: At seasonal and occasional family banquets, offer wine and a blessing to the head of the family, bow, and wait for his command to sit.
items.quote: 上夀於家長卑幼盛服序立如朔望之儀先再拜……家長命諸卑幼坐 — At banquets, juniors in full dress offer wine and blessing to the family head, bow, and wait for his command to sit.

items.text: Educate your children according to their age and sex: teach respect for elders, numbers, directions, reading, and household skills; firmly correct disrespect.
items.quote: 稍有知則教之以恭敬尊長……六嵗教之數與方名男子始習書字女始習女工之小者 — When the child has some understanding, teach respect for elders; at six teach numbers and directions; boys begin writing, girls small needlework.

items.text: Rise at cockcrow, wash and dress; sweep the house and hall; when the master and mistress arise, smooth the bed, fold covers, and stand ready to serve; prepare food and do all tasks as ordered.
items.quote: 凡内外僕妾鷄初鳴咸起櫛總盥漱衣服男僕灑掃㕔事及庭……主父主母既起則拂牀襞衾侍立左右以備使令 — Servants rise at cockcrow, wash and dress; male servants sweep; when master and mistress arise, they smooth the bed, fold covers, and stand ready to serve.

items.text: Perform your son's capping ceremony between ages fifteen and twenty, but only if you have no mourning of a year or more; choose a worthy guest to instruct him.
items.quote: 男子年十五至二十皆可冠……必父母無朞以上喪始可行之 — A son may be capped between fifteen and twenty, but only if parents have no mourning of a year or more.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷五 · 51 · 前一月下旬卜日 … 辭神乃徹而退

items.text: Choose an auspicious day by divination in the latter part of the previous month for the sacrifice to your deceased parents.
items.quote: 前一月下旬卜日 — In the latter part of the previous month, divine the day.
items.conflict: Divination is forbidden; seek God's guidance through His Word and prayer (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: Purify yourself by abstinence for three days before the sacrifice to your deceased parents.
items.quote: 前三日齋戒 — For three days beforehand, keep abstinence.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; worship belongs to God alone (Exod. 20:3-5).

items.text: Prepare the place, vessels, and food offerings as for the seasonal sacrifice.
items.quote: 前一日設位陳器 — On the previous day, set the places and arrange the vessels.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Bring out the spirit tablet and place it in the main hall, then perform the offerings with reverence and grief.
items.quote: 詣祠堂奉神主出就正寝 — Go to the shrine, bring out the spirit tablet, and proceed to the main hall.
items.conflict: Making offerings to spirit tablets is idolatry; the dead are not present to receive worship (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: Offer the first libation and recite the prayer expressing unending longing.
items.quote: 感時追慕昊天罔極 — Moved by the season, I recall with unending longing.
items.conflict: Prayers to the dead are necromancy; pray to God alone (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: On the anniversary of a parent's death, abstain from wine, meat, and music, wear plain clothes, and sleep outside.
items.quote: 是日不飲酒不食肉不聼樂 — On that day do not drink wine, eat meat, or listen to music.

items.text: On the anniversary, perform the offering but do not receive the blessing portion or share the food.
items.quote: 亞獻終獻〔並如祭禰之儀但不受胙〕 — The second and third offerings: as in the sacrifice to a father, but do not receive the blessing portion.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: At the grave, sweep the area, remove weeds, and walk around the tomb three times in sorrow.
items.quote: 環繞哀省三周 — Circle the tomb three times in sorrow.
items.conflict: Tomb sweeping as a rite to the dead is necromantic; honor the dead by remembering them, but do not serve them (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: Offer the food and libations at the grave, reciting the prayer of remembrance.
items.quote: 瞻掃封塋不勝感慕 — I look and sweep the mound, overcome with longing.
items.conflict: Offerings and prayers to the dead are forbidden; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Assist in the second and third libations at the grave.
items.quote: 亞獻終獻〔並以子弟親賓為之〕 — The second and third offerings are made by sons, younger brothers, and relatives.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; worship belongs to God alone.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 160 · 叅神 … 父母亡答人䟽

items.text: Offer the sacrificial rites of greeting and descent of spirits, presenting food and the first cup to the ancestors and the newly deceased.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 叅神〔在位者皆再拜〓祖考妣〕
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5 prohibits worship of anyone but God.

items.text: When your husband is the chief mourner, make the second offering (亞獻) in the ancestral rite.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 若宗子自為喪主則主婦為亞獻
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5 prohibits worship of anyone but God.

items.text: Before the小祥, lead the men of the household to sweep and purify the house in preparation for the rite.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 主人帥衆丈夫灑掃滌濯

items.text: Before the小祥, lead the women of the household to wash the vessels and prepare the sacrificial food.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 主婦帥衆婦女滌釜鼎具祭饌

items.text: During the three-year mourning for a parent, do not converse or ask questions; speak only of necessary matters.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 三年之喪言而不語對而不問

items.text: While mourning a parent, do not laugh or show your teeth as a sign of grief.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 高子臯執親之喪未嘗見齒

items.text: During the mourning period for a parent, refrain from bathing except at the prescribed times.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 凡喪小功以上非虞祔練祥無沐浴

items.text: At the大祥, announce the transfer of the spirit tablet to the ancestral hall and perform the offerings.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 告遷於祠堂
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5 prohibits worship of anyone but God.

items.text: Refrain from wine, meat, and normal sleeping arrangements until after the大祥 rite is completed.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 始飯酒食肉而復寢

items.text: Before the final mourning rite, divine the day by casting shells before the tablet of your deceased father, seeking his approval.
items.citation: Jiali, 卷四 160 叅神…父母亡答人疏
items.quote: 主人炷香燻珓命以上旬之日
items.conflict: Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids divination and consulting the dead.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 196 · 某稽顙再拜言 … 進饌

items.text: When a relative has lost a parent, do not wait for him to write; send a letter of condolence to share his grief.
items.quote: 凡遭父母喪知舊不以書來弔問是無相恤之心 — If one has lost a parent and a friend or acquaintance does not send a letter of condolence, he lacks a sympathizing heart.

items.text: When you have received a letter of condolence, send a respectful letter of thanks in return.
items.quote: 伏䝉尊慈俯賜慰問哀感之至 — I have received your kind condolence; my grief is touched to the utmost.

items.text: Lead the men of the house in three days of purification before the seasonal sacrifice, abstaining from meat, mourning, and music.
items.quote: 前期三日主人帥衆丈夫致齋於外沐浴更衣飲酒不得至亂食肉不得茹葷不弔喪不聼樂 — Three days before, the master leads all the men to keep vigil outside; they bathe and change clothes, do not drink to excess, do not eat meat or strong-smelling vegetables, do not visit mourners, and do not listen to music.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden; fasting for it is part of idolatry (Exodus 20:4-5; Deuteronomy 26:14).

items.text: Lead the women of the house in the same three days of purification, with the same abstinences.
items.quote: 主婦帥衆婦女致齋於内沐浴更衣飲酒不得至亂食肉不得茹葷不弔喪不聼樂 — The mistress leads all the women to keep vigil inside; they bathe and change clothes, do not drink to excess, do not eat meat or strong-smelling vegetables, do not visit mourners, and do not listen to music.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden; participation in its purification is sin (Psalm 106:28).

items.text: Lead the men of the house in sweeping, cleaning, and setting out the ritual places and vessels for the ancestors.
items.quote: 主人帥衆丈夫深衣及執事灑掃正〓洗拭倚卓務令蠲潔 — The master leads all the men in deep robes and the attendants to sweep, wipe, and clean the seats and tables, making them spotless.
items.conflict: Preparing for idolatrous sacrifice is sinful (1 Corinthians 10:20-21).

items.text: Lead the women of the house in washing the sacrificial vessels and preparing the food offerings.
items.quote: 主婦帥衆婦女背子滌濯祭器潔釜鼎具祭饌 — The mistress leads all the women in upper garments to wash the sacrificial vessels, clean the pots, and prepare the offerings.
items.conflict: Preparing food for offerings to the dead is forbidden (Deuteronomy 26:14; Isaiah 8:19).

items.text: As the filial descendant, announce to the ancestors' spirit tablets that you are performing the seasonal offering, and ask their spirits to come forth to the main hall.
items.quote: 孝孫某今以仲春之月有事於皇高祖考...敢請神主出就正寢恭伸奠獻 — Your filial descendant will this month perform the service to the ancestors; I dare ask the spirit tablets to come forth to the main hall for the offering.
items.conflict: Addressing or invoking the dead is forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Isaiah 8:19).

items.text: All members of the house must bow before the ancestor spirits as they are received.
items.quote: 主人以下叙立如祠堂之儀立定再拜 — From the master down, they stand in order as in the ancestral hall; when composed, they bow twice.
items.conflict: Bowing to the dead is idolatry (Exodus 20:5; Revelation 22:8-9).

items.text: Pour out a libation of wine on the grass to summon the spirits of the ancestors to descend.
items.quote: 主人左手執盤右手執盞灌於茅上 — The master with left hand holds the dish and right hand holds the cup, and pours the wine upon the grass.
items.conflict: Libation to spirits is offering to demons (Deuteronomy 32:17; Psalm 106:37).

items.text: Present the meat, fish, and broth before the place of each ancestor.
items.quote: 主人搢笏奉肉奠於盤盞之南...主人奉魚奠於醋碟之南...主人奉羮奠於醋碟之東 — The master presents the meat south of the dish, the fish south of the vinegar saucer, and the broth east of the vinegar saucer.
items.conflict: Offering food to the dead is forbidden (Deuteronomy 26:14; Psalm 106:28).

items.text: Present the noodles, rice, and cooked food before the place of each ancestor.
items.quote: 主婦奉麫食奠於肉西...主婦奉米食奠於魚東...主婦奉飯奠於盤盞之西 — The mistress presents the flour food west of the meat, the rice food east of the fish, and the cooked rice west of the dish and cup.
items.conflict: Offering food to the dead is forbidden (Deuteronomy 26:14; Psalm 106:28).

items.text: Divine an auspicious day for the seasonal sacrifice by casting the divination blocks before the ancestors.
items.quote: 主人搢笏焚香薰珓而命以上旬之日...即以珓擲於盤以一俯一仰為吉 — The master burns incense and casts the divination blocks, naming a day in the first ten days; he throws the blocks on the dish, and one up and one down is lucky.
items.conflict: Divination is forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Leviticus 19:26).

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷五 · 11 · 初獻 … 季秋祭禰

items.text: Offer the first wine and read the prayer at each ancestor's place in due order, bowing before them.
items.quote: 主人升詣高祖位前...執事者西向斟酒...主人奉之奠於故處 — The host ascends to the place of the high ancestor, pours wine, and places it.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: Offer the second wine and the roasted meat, as the host does but without reading the prayer.
items.quote: 亞獻〔主婦為之諸婦女奉炙肉及分獻如初獻儀但不讀祝〕 — The wife performs the second offering; the women present roasted meat, as in the first offering but without reading the prayer.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: Offer the third wine; if you are not the eldest, then the eldest brother or eldest son or a close relative should do it.
items.quote: 終獻〔兄弟之長或長男或親賓為之〕 — The eldest brother, eldest son, or a relative performs the final offering.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: Assist in the offerings at the attached positions and present the meat, but do not read the prayer.
items.quote: 兄弟衆男...分詣本位所祔之位酌獻如儀但不讀祝 — The younger brothers and sons go to the attached places and pour offerings in order, but do not read the prayer.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: With your wife, serve wine, food, and tea before the ancestors; close the door while they eat and open it after.
items.quote: 主人升...就斟諸位之酒皆滿...主人主婦奉茶分進於考妣之前 — The host fills wine at each place; host and wife present tea before the ancestors.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: Return the spirit tablets to the shrine and put them away in their chest.
items.quote: 主人主婦皆升各奉主納於櫝 — Host and wife carry the tablets and return them to the shrine.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; idolatry.

items.text: Send a portion of the sacrificial meat to relatives and friends.
items.quote: 遣僕執書歸胙於親友 — Send a servant with a letter to bring sacrificial meat to relatives and friends.
items.conflict: Part of ancestor worship; food offered to idols.

items.text: Offer wine and bow to the elder who sits first at the feast; hear his blessing.
items.quote: 衆男叙立...皆再拜子弟之長者一人少進立...獻者搢笏跪...授執盞者置於尊者之前 — The young men stand in rows and bow; one young man offers wine and places it before the elder.
items.conflict: Part of ancestor worship feast.

items.text: Share the blessing and order wine for all the young men; then drink with them.
items.quote: 尊者命取注及長者之盞置於前自斟之...命執事者以次就位斟酒皆徧長者進跪受飲 — The elder orders wine for all, and the young men drink.
items.conflict: Part of ancestor worship feast.

items.text: Distribute the sacrificial meat to the servants and hired hands, both inside and outside, so that all receive it.
items.quote: 主人頒胙於外僕主婦頒胙於内執事者徧及㣲賤 — The host distributes to outside servants, the wife to inside servants, reaching even the lowly.
items.conflict: Food offered to idols; see 1 Corinthians 8.

items.text: Perform the sacrifices with love and respect; if poor or ill, do according to your means and strength, but do not neglect them.
items.quote: 凡祭主於盡愛敬之誠而已貧則稱家之有無疾則量筋力而行之 — In sacrifice, the main thing is to exhaust love and respect; if poor, according to means; if ill, according to strength.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry.

items.text: Only the legitimate heir of the family may sacrifice to his direct ancestors; branch sons must not offer these rites.
items.quote: 繼禰之宗以上皆得祭惟支子不祭 — Only the heir from the ancestor at one's own level may sacrifice; branch sons may not.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry; also usurping the priestly role.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷一 · 11 · 有事則告 … 凡為人子者出必告反必面有賓客不敢

items.text: When any significant event occurs—such as receiving an office, a promotion, a demotion, a posthumous honor, or the birth of an eldest son—report it to the ancestors at the shrine, offering tea and wine.
items.quote: 有事則告 — When there is an event, report it.

items.text: If fire, flood, or thieves threaten, first rescue the ancestral shrine, spirit tablets, and sacrificial vessels before saving family property.
items.quote: 先救祠堂遷神主遺書次及祭器然後及家財 — First save the ancestral shrine, move the spirit tablets and writings, next the sacrificial vessels, then family property.

items.text: As heir of the main line, keep the grave land and offer yearly sacrifices at the tombs of the ancestors without fail.
items.quote: 大宗猶主其墓田以奉其墓祭嵗率宗人一祭之百世不改 — The main-line heir keeps the grave land to perform the tomb sacrifices, leading the clan yearly without change.

items.text: Govern all younger members and household servants by the rites and laws, assign each one duties, hold them to account, manage income and expenses, provide clothing and food to all according to their station, cut waste, forbid extravagance, and keep a reserve for emergencies.
items.quote: 謹守禮法以御羣子弟及家衆分之以職授之以事而責其成功制財用之節量入以為出稱家之有無以給上下之衣食

items.text: In all matters, great or small, do not act on your own; first ask and report to the head of the household.
items.quote: 事無大小毋得専行必咨禀於家長 — In matters great or small, do not act on your own; always ask the head of the household.

items.text: Keep no private wealth; hand over all income from salary or land to your parents, and when you need something, ask before using it; do not lend or give privately.
items.quote: 毋得蓄私財俸禄及田宅所入盡歸之父母 — Do not keep private wealth; all income from salary and land goes to your parents.

items.text: Keep no private wealth; hand over all income to your parents-in-law, and ask before using anything; do not lend or give privately.
items.quote: 盡歸之父母舅姑 — Give all to parents and parents-in-law.

items.text: Rise at dawn, wash, dress, and go to your parents to ask how they are; in the evening see them settled before retiring; when going out, tell them, and when returning, report to them.
items.quote: 出必告反必面 — When going out, tell them; when returning, report.

items.text: Prepare and give your parents any medicine they need yourself; do not leave it to servants.
items.quote: 供藥物...不可但委婢僕 — Provide medicine... do not just relegate it to servants.

items.text: Prepare the morning meal for your parents-in-law, ensuring it is clean and well-made.
items.quote: 婦具晨羞...務令精潔 — The wife prepares the morning food... make it clean and pure.

items.text: Record your parents' instructions, carry them out promptly, and report back when done; if an order seems wrong, explain gently and seek their consent; if they persist in error, remonstrate with respect, even if they become angry.
items.quote: 受父母之命必籍記而佩之...父母有過下氣怡色柔聲以諫

items.text: Do not use wealth or official rank to behave proudly toward your father or clan elders, and do not sit in the main hall, use the eastern steps, or in any way set yourself up as your father's equal.
items.quote: 不敢以貴富加於父兄宗族...凡事不敢自擬於其父 — Do not use wealth or rank to add to father or clan elders... in nothing presume to equal your father.

heading: 家禮 Jiali · Family Rituals (Zhu Xi) · 家禮 卷四 · 53 · 凡為殤服以次降一等 … 遂穿壙

items.text: Mourn your natal relatives one degree lower than the usual grades, because you have become heir to another line.
items.quote: 凡男為人後...為其私親皆降一等 — A man adopted as heir elsewhere mourns his own kin one degree lower.

items.text: Mourn your natal kin one degree lower; if divorced before mourning ends, resume full mourning.
items.quote: 女適人者為其私親皆降一等...未滿被出則服其本服 — A daughter who marries out mourns her own kin one degree lower; if divorced before completion, she resumes the original mourning.

items.text: While mourning your parent, eat only congee or coarse food according to your relation, and do not go out or join banquets except for funeral needs.
items.quote: 成服之日主人及兄弟始食粥...不食菜菓...飲酒食肉不與宴樂 — The mourners first eat congee... those in five- and three-month mourning may drink wine and eat meat but do not join banquets.

items.text: Every morning and evening, present food, incense, and wine before the spirit tablet, bow, and weep; offer also at mealtimes, new moon, and when new produce is available.
items.quote: 朝夕哭奠上食朝奠...朔日則於朝奠設饌...有新物則薦之 — Morning and evening offerings with weeping, food at mealtimes, on the first of the month set out dishes, and when there is new produce, present it.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are vain and violate biblical worship.

items.text: When you come to condole, wear plain white mourning clothes, bring incense, wine, fruit, and a gift, announce yourself, then weep, make libation, and console the mourner.
items.quote: 凡弔皆素服...奠用香茶燭酒果...賻用錢帛...入哭奠訖乃弔而退 — All who condole wear white... offerings of incense, tea, candles, wine, fruit... gifts of money and silk... weep and offer, then console and leave.

items.text: On hearing of your parent's death, weep, put on mourning clothes, hasten home, and upon arrival bow before the coffin and mourn.
items.quote: 始聞親喪哭...易服...遂行...入門詣柩前再拜 — On first hearing of a parent's death, wail... change clothes... set out... enter and bow twice before the coffin.

items.text: When you hear of the death of a relative for whom you wear mourning, set up a spirit seat and weep; if you cannot go, do so on the fourth day and monthly until the period ends.
items.quote: 齊衰以下聞喪為位而哭...若不奔喪則四日成服...毎月朔為位會哭 — For mourning of one year or less, upon hearing the death, set up a place and wail... if not traveling, assume mourning on the fourth day... on each first day of the month set up a place and wail together.

items.text: Bury your parent within three months; choose a plot that is deep, dry, and safe from roads and plows, not for geomantic gain.
items.quote: 三月而葬前期擇地...故必求土厚小深之地而葬之所以不可不擇也 — Bury in three months; beforehand choose the ground... seek deep, thick soil that is not shallow or damp.

items.text: Do not cremate your parent's remains; bury the body whole, for burning it destroys what a filial child should cherish.
items.quote: 世人又有遊宦沒於逺方子孫火焚其柩收燼歸葬者...殘毁它人之尸在律猶嚴况子孫乃悖謬如此 — Some sons burn their father's coffin afar... mutilating another's body is severely punished by law; how much more wrong for a son.

items.text: Before digging the grave, have a deputy announce to the earth god and offer wine and food, praying for protection.
items.quote: 擇日開塋域祠后土...告后土氏...敢告於后土氏之神...神其保佑 — Choose a day, open the grave plot, sacrifice to the earth god... announce to the spirit of the earth... may the spirit protect.
items.conflict: Sacrifice to a local earth god violates the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3).
